description: Create a seat of your own, list the seats, or close one. A seat has its own pointer, keyboard, focus and clipboard, its own outputs and workspaces, and its own Wayland socket, which the programs it starts use; no input, focus or clipboard of one seat reaches another. Create one first: every other tool but clock takes its handle, rest when it is to name only that seat's. Closing it releases what it holds, disconnects its windows, ends its programs (SIGTERM and SIGCONT, then SIGKILL 2 s later) and removes its outputs; it answers once they are gone, in 3 s at most. A Yuna on a manual clock holds one seat.

hdr.description: create: true announces the HDR colours of the owner's monitor, a PG32UCDM; false, SDR; by default as the server's default output

scale.description: create: physical pixels per logical unit; default 1.5

vrr_min.description: create: run under VRR, from this many refreshes a second up to rate, which must be at least twice it; by default a fixed rate, or the server's default output's range when rate is left out too

width.description: create: its output's physical pixels; default 3840

name: seat
title: Seats

description: List, create, configure or remove a seat's virtual outputs: screens no monitor shows, drawn at their own size, rate and scale, at a fixed rate or under VRR, announcing SDR or HDR colours. Windows open on the seat's focused output. Coordinates are logical: physical pixels divided by the scale. A seat keeps one output at least. An output's side is 8192 pixels at most, and Yuna's outputs, every seat's, hold 132710400 pixels at most together, those of 16 at 3840 × 2160. list gives each output's VRR range in Hz and the monitor whose HDR colours it announces, each null when it has none. configure changes an output as a monitor set to another mode, whole or not at all: it keeps its top-left corner, the seat's outputs on its right move with its right edge so that none overlaps it, and its windows are placed again in it; X11 windows keep the scale their X server started with. create and configure answer with the output as list gives it.

hdr.description: create: true announces the HDR colours of the owner's monitor, a PG32UCDM; false, SDR; by default as the server's default output; configure: the output's own by default

height.description: create: physical pixels; default 2160; configure: the output's own by default

rate.description: create: refreshes a second; default 240; configure: the output's own by default

scale.description: create: physical pixels per logical unit; default 1.5; configure: the output's own by default

vrr_min.description: create: run under VRR, from this many refreshes a second up to rate, which must be at least twice it; by default a fixed rate, or the server's default output's range when rate is left out too; configure: the output's own by default, kept when rate changes; 0 runs it at a fixed rate

width.description: create: physical pixels; default 3840; configure: the output's own by default

name: outputs
title: Virtual outputs

description: List a seat's workspaces by output, with their windows; create or remove a named one; show one; or move a window to one, created if needed. A removed workspace keeps its windows, unnamed.

name.description: create, remove, focus: the workspace's name, 256 bytes at most in UTF-8

output.description: create: the output it lives on; the focused one by default

workspace.description: move_window: the workspace's name, 256 bytes at most in UTF-8

name: workspaces
title: Workspaces

description: Start a program on a seat, list a seat's programs, stop one, read its log, or make it stuck or slow. A program gets its seat's Wayland socket and X display, an environment without Yuna's own DISPLAY or the user's D-Bus, and a log of its output and errors; its windows open on its seat. It runs on its seat's throwaway home, never the user's: HOME names a folder the seat's programs share, removed when the seat closes, with XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME inside it; a variable named in env wins, to give a program a test profile, or the user's own home on purpose. env {"WAYLAND_DEBUG": "client"} writes its Wayland trace to its log. list gives each program's state, its log's size, its run_percent (100 free, 0 frozen) and protocol_error: the last Wayland protocol error one of its connections was ended for (interface, object, code, message), null for none. stop sends its process group SIGTERM then SIGCONT, or SIGKILL with force. log gives text, the bytes from to to of its output as UTF-8, invalid bytes replaced: max_bytes of them, 64 KiB by default, 1 MiB at most, from the byte offset from since it started, or its newest without from; size is every byte it wrote, dropped those its log did not keep: a log keeps its first 256 KiB and its newest 1 MiB; ended is true once its output has closed. freeze stops its process group (SIGSTOP) until thaw continues it (SIGCONT); slow lets it run run_percent of each 100 ms and stops it the rest, on real time whatever the clock, until thaw, freeze, stop or the end of its group. A frozen program reads no event: once its Wayland socket's buffer fills, Yuna closes its connection, and events tells client_left with reason closed. Logs go when the seat closes. With accessibility, it joins its seat's accessibility bus, which the first such program starts, and the accessibility tool reads its tree: GTK, Qt and the ATK bridge's toolkits turn their accessibility on; Chromium and Electron also need --force-renderer-accessibility in their command for a page's own content. Without it, a program runs with its toolkit's accessibility off.

accessibility.description: start: on its seat's accessibility bus, its tree read by the accessibility tool; false by default

command.description: start: the program, found in PATH, and its arguments

env.description: start: variables added to its environment

from.description: log: the first byte, an offset since it started; its newest bytes by default

max_bytes.description: log: how many bytes at most; 65536 by default

program.description: stop, log, freeze, thaw, slow: the program's id

run_percent.description: slow: the share of each 100 ms it runs

name: spawn
title: Programs

description: List a seat's windows, in the order they opened: id, seat, shell (xdg for a Wayland program's window, x11 for an X11 program's), application id (an X11 window's WM_CLASS class; null when its client gave none), title, process id, output, workspace (null for an unnamed one), rect: the logical rectangle it is drawn at now, or where its output's last frame drew it when that frame was sampled later (null when its output's frame does not draw it), place: its rectangle in the layout, where it rests once its motion ends (null when hidden), motion_ends_ns: when its output's motion ends, on the clock's scale (null at rest), focus, floating, fullscreen, unresponsive: an X11 window asked to close that left its ping unanswered 5 s. With neither --animations nor --reduced-motion, rect is place and motion_ends_ns null. With colour, each window also gives colours: one entry for each of its surfaces that declared its colours through color-management-v1, its own, then its subsurfaces' and its popups': the surface's role, transfer function, primaries (a protocol name, else their chromaticities), luminances in cd/m², target primaries and luminance, max_cll, max_fall and rendering intent. With wait_ms, waits up to that long for a window that matches the filters, when none does yet.

colour.description: also give the colours each window's surfaces declared; false by default

wait_ms.description: how long to wait for a match; 0 by default

name: windows
title: Windows

description: Wait for what happens on a seat, or read what happened since a cursor, rather than asking in a loop. Each event gives seq, a number that grows across the whole Yuna and is never reused, time_ns on the clock's scale, kind, and its fields; a title, an app_id or a workspace is cut to 512 bytes. Yuna looks for events at the end of each round, and at each events call, so that one without after waits only for what comes after it; a window is told at most once a look. Kinds: window_opened (window, app_id, title, pid, shell); window_closed (window); window_changed (window, title, app_id: either changed, however often since the last look); window_placed (window, output, workspace, place: where it rests in the layout changed, told once the layout is arranged); window_unresponsive (window: it left a ping unanswered, as windows' unresponsive tells); focus (window: the seat's focus moved, null for none); program_exited (program, exit_code or signal, the other null); client_left (pid, program, reason, error: a Wayland connection of the seat ended; reason protocol_error, with error's interface, object, code and message, or closed, error null: it left, sent what is not Wayland, or could not take its events; pid as windows gives it; program null for a client of no program, or one whose process had exited before Yuna accepted it); client_refused (bound, refused: the seat's socket closed connections at once, the seat serving bound clients already, its Xwayland apart; refused counts them since the seat's last client_refused; told at the first refusal, then at the first a second or more after the last told: the refusals after the last told wait for such a refusal, and are not told if none comes); output_added, output_removed, output_changed (output). With after, a seq or a reply's next, gives the events after it, only kinds when given, at most 256 a reply; next is the cursor to give next, and missed how many events of the seat after the cursor its log, which keeps its last 1024, dropped. Without after, no past event: the reply's next reads what comes. With wait_ms, waits up to that long, on real time whatever the clock, for a first event that matches, and answers once the round that recorded it ends, or at once when the log dropped events after the cursor; timed_out is true when none came. A window that opens and closes between two looks is not seen. Yuna keeps nothing between calls: the cursor is yours.

after.description: the cursor: an event's seq or a reply's next; none for what comes from now

kinds.description: only these kinds; every kind by default

wait_ms.description: how long to wait for a first event; 0 by default

name: events
title: Events

description: Find nodes of the accessibility trees of a seat's programs started with spawn start and accessibility: true, a button by its name for one: each node's window, app (its process id), role and name as AT-SPI gives them, description, states, and rect, its rectangle in its output's logical units from the output's top-left corner, the units pointer takes: click its centre to press it. name is a part of the node's name, compared without regard to case; role an AT-SPI role name (button, check box, text, frame, label…); states AT-SPI state names the node must all have (focused, checked, sensitive, showing…). window or pid limit the walk to that program's tree. A walk visits max_nodes nodes at most, 10000 by default, and gives 256 nodes at most, more true past them; each program has 3 s to answer, and one that does not is told so in apps, never holding the others. With wait_ms, waits up to that long for a node that matches, walking again as the programs change. A program started without accessibility is not on the bus.

max_nodes.description: the most nodes visited; 10000 by default

name.description: a part of the name, any case

states.description: AT-SPI state names the node must all have

wait_ms.description: how long to wait for a match; 0 by default

name: accessibility
title: Accessibility tree

description: Capture what one of a seat's outputs shows, as a PNG image of its newest frame: the one being drawn when a change is on its way, else the last one drawn. All of the output, its first by default, a region of it, or a window: what the output shows where the window is, what covers it included; a hidden window is refused. By default at the logical size, where a pixel is a logical unit, the units pointer takes; size physical gives every physical pixel. The result tells how the image maps to its output, logical = x + pixel × units_per_pixel, and gives a capture id: pointer takes it, with x and y in that image's pixels. One capture of a seat at a time. It comes once the clock reaches the boundary its frame is presented at: on a manual clock, advance it.

output.description: the output; the seat's first by default

region.description: a rectangle of the output, in whole logical units from its top-left corner

window.description: a window's id, instead of an output or a region

name: capture
title: Capture

description: Move, press, release, click or scroll a seat's pointer, or read where it is. x and y are logical units from the top-left corner of one of the seat's outputs, its first by default, which are a whole output's capture's pixels at the logical size; with capture, they are pixels of that capture's image, which Yuna maps to its output. press, release, click and scroll move first when x and y are given. A press focuses the window under it. Drag in several calls: press, move, release. The result tells where the pointer is, in the output's logical units whatever x and y were given in, the window under it and the position on its surface, and the cursor its client last asked for, before it handled this call's input.

button.description: press, release, click: left by default

capture.description: a capture's id, among the seat's last 16: x and y are pixels of its image, instead of an output's units

output.description: the output x and y are on

name: pointer
title: Pointer

description: Press, release or tap keys on a seat's keyboard, type text, show text being composed, or change its layout, to the window its keyboard is on, or read where it is. Keys are named as XKB names them: Return, a, F5, BackSpace, Left; a name presses a key that types that keysym, alone where one does, and adds no modifier. tap takes keys joined by +, the last pressed while the others are held: ctrl+shift+t; ctrl, shift, alt, super and altgr name modifiers. type types text through the seat's layout, us unless changed, with Shift, AltGr and the layout's own switch between its layouts, any character included: one its keys do not type is committed to the text field there when it speaks text-input-v3. preedit shows text being composed in that text field, as an input method does, until the next type replaces it; empty text clears it. layout sets the seat's XKB layout, variant and options, on the evdev rules and a pc105 keyboard: fr, or us,ru with the option grp:alt_shift_toggle; every program of the seat gets the new keymap; it is refused while a key is held, and for a layout, variant or option XKB's rules do not know. The result tells the window the keyboard is on and whether a text field is enabled there; get's and layout's tell the seat's layout, variant and options too. A click focuses a window; the keyboard follows it at the output's next refresh.

layout.description: layout: XKB's layouts, joined by commas, four at most: fr, us,ru; 256 bytes at most in UTF-8

options.description: layout: XKB's options, joined by commas, such as grp:alt_shift_toggle; none when left out; 256 bytes at most in UTF-8

text.description: type: the text; preedit: the text being composed

variant.description: layout: their variants, one for each layout, joined by commas; each layout's default when left out; 256 bytes at most in UTF-8

name: keyboard
title: Keyboard

description: Read, set or clear a seat's clipboard, or its primary selection, which its X11 and Wayland programs copy to and paste from alike. get gives the MIME types the selection offers, none when it is empty, and the data of one of them, mime, by default the first text type it offers of text/plain;charset=utf-8, UTF8_STRING, text/plain, STRING, TEXT, null when it offers none: as text when it is UTF-8 with no control character but tab, newline and carriage return, else in base64 with base64 true; at most max_bytes, with truncated when there was more. It waits for the program that copied to write the data, 5 s at most, then answers with what came and timed_out. set holds the selection for you, offering text as text/plain;charset=utf-8, text/plain, UTF8_STRING, until a program copies something else or clear; a program pastes it while its window has the seat's keyboard, as any paste. clear empties the selection, whoever copied it.

max_bytes.description: get: the most bytes of data given; 65536 by default

mime.description: get: the MIME type to read, one the selection offers

selection.description: clipboard by default; primary is the selection a middle click pastes

text.description: set: the text, 262144 bytes at most in UTF-8; the request's line, the text escaped as JSON included, is 1048576 bytes at most

name: clipboard
title: Clipboard

description: Read Yuna's clock, on CLOCK_MONOTONIC's scale, in nanoseconds; or advance it, when Yuna was started with --manual-clock, running every frame due on the way. It never moves past real time. It is the whole Yuna's.
name: clock
title: Clock

description: Name what woke Yuna and what made it draw: at rest, nothing does. Without wait_ms, what was counted since Yuna started; with wait_ms, what is counted in the next wait_ms of real time, whatever the clock, answered at its end, this call's own timer left out, and the wake it caused when nothing else woke Yuna with it; this call's request came before that window and its reply goes after it. The timer of --rest-audit's log is never counted, in a window or since Yuna started. It counts among the calls that wait, and fails when its seat closes. since_ns and now_ns are the counts' start and end on the clock's scale. wakes: the times Yuna woke, every seat's. sources: each source that woke it, with how many times: clients, seat_socket, socket_pause, clock_refresh, clock_presentation, clock_hidden_frames, clock_x11_answers, clock_drags, stop_signal, child_ended, mcp_input, mcp_output, encoders, program_output, programs_throttle, program_pace, seat_closing, waiting_call, capture_timeout, capture_boundary, xwayland_timeout, xwayland_pause, x11_connection, xwayland_display, xwayland_exited, x11_manager, accessibility_bus, accessibility_daemon, accessibility_address, accessibility_log, accessibility_start, accessibility_call, clipboard_read, clipboard_read_timeout, selection_write, selection_write_timeout. clients: each client that woke Yuna or made it draw, with pid, program (null for none), seat, xwayland (its seat's Xwayland, the client of every X11 program there), wakes (times it had something to send when the clients woke Yuna), commits and draws (frames drawn with one of its commits among their causes); clients_gone: the same for the clients that left, together, with their count; unnamed_client_wakes: the clients' wakes in which Yuna named none, out of descriptors. programs: each program whose output (output_wakes) or pace (pace_wakes) woke Yuna. frames: the frames drawn; draw_causes: each cause with its frames, a frame counted under each of its causes: commit, layout_change, motion, capture, first_frame, output_change, popups. With seat, only that seat's clients, programs, sockets, outputs' refreshes, Xwayland, accessibility bus and clipboard reads and writes, beside Yuna's own parts: signals, MCP's input and output, encoders, waiting calls, captures' timers, the programs' throttle, the hidden windows' frames, X11 answers and drags' time limits; wakes and unnamed_client_wakes stay every seat's, an unnamed wake's client, and so its seat, being unknown.

seat.description: only this seat's, beside Yuna's own parts; every seat's by default

wait_ms.description: count this long from now and answer then; by default, what was counted since Yuna started

name: rest
title: Rest audit
